stories.title: The Hour of His Taking
stories.fortuneLine: You bought a dusk that will not fall, and the clock will collect it from your bones.
stories.body:
A man was given the hour of his taking, inked on the inside of his wrist.

He found a clock standing in a parlor already underwater, a bird with one burning eye upon the crown.

The bargain did not need a mouth.
He paid in evenings.
Dusk lifted from the valley and did not return.
The hands learned to rest at ten and two, and would not close.

Years of afternoon.
The writing on his wrist faded.
The rooms forgot their names.

When his fingers failed the key, he sat in the black water and waited for the taking.

The pendulum kept its little law without him.
It had not been keeping his hours.
It had been keeping the debt.

Where twelve should have been, a thirteenth mark.
Beneath it, the word the maker set before the first winding.

The bird bent to the keyhole and gave the works their name.

Never.
